samples.summary: Width-forwarding in text-renderer's dash call is untested (fixture uses width 1, where scaling is a no-op)
samples.evidence: `text-renderer.ts:153` now calls `dashArray(data.stroke.dash, data.stroke.width)`, but the only dash test for it (`text-renderer.test.ts:210-218`) strokes `width: 1` and asserts the literal `[6, 4]`. Since `dashArray(dash, 1) === dashArray(dash)`, this assertion passes identically if the width argument were dropped — the change to this painter has no test that can fail. Contrast `stroke-dash.test.ts`, which deliberately uses `STROKE_W = 2` so the shape/connector/action-button/placeholder paths do catch a missing width.

samples.summary: No test at all covers table cell-border dashing, including the new width-scaled call
samples.evidence: `paintCellBorders` was changed to `dashArray(edge.stroke.dash, edge.stroke.width)`, but a grep for `dash` across `packages/slides/test` returns no table-renderer file, and `src/view/canvas/stroke-dash.test.ts` only exercises `drawShape` and `drawConnector`. A regression that dropped the width (or the dash entirely) on table borders would ship green.

samples.summary: Dash round-trip coverage is shape-only; connector strokes (which share parseShapeStroke) have no import/round-trip dash assertion
samples.evidence: The new round-trip case builds three `type: 'shape'` elements and the new importer unit tests in `test/import/pptx/shape.test.ts` use a `<p:sp>` fixture only. `parseCxnSp` (src/import/pptx/shape.ts:1054) also consumes `parseShapeStroke`, and connectors are the element most likely to carry a dash, yet no test asserts a dashed connector survives export→import. The shared helper makes this low-risk, which is why it is minor rather than major.
searchedFor: read test/export/pptx/round-trip.test.ts imports and new case

samples.summary: Preview assertions are derived from `dashArray` itself, so they cannot detect a wrong pattern — only a wrong width argument
samples.evidence: Lines 42-47, 60-62 and 131-133 compare the rendered `stroke-dasharray` to `dashArray(...)` output. If `dashArray` itself regressed, these stay green. The width-16 and 4px cases do pin the width argument (a clamped/ignored width would mismatch), and `render-context.test.ts:134-145` pins the literals, so the composite coverage is adequate; flagging only that the frontend file alone proves less than its comment claims.
